key_insight: A closed-form harmonic model predicts oscillating-foil forces and power from motion inputs, linking higher harmonics to discrete vortex-shedding events.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a fast alternative to high-fidelity simulations for renewable-energy foil design and array optimization.
method: Generate 405 two-dimensional simulations spanning heave amplitude, pitch amplitude, and frequency.
Decompose lift and pitching moment into odd Fourier harmonics.
Regress harmonic coefficients on 16 physics-based polynomial terms using separate Ridge steps for attribution and prediction.
evidence_signal: The model achieves leave-one-out R² = 0.98 for cycle-averaged power, with median instantaneous-lift peak error of 9% and phase error below 1% of a period.
watch_item: Validation is based on two-dimensional simulations; accuracy for three-dimensional devices or motions outside the sampled parameter space remains unestablished.
paper_title: Harmonic structure and parametric prediction of instantaneous power in oscillating foils
